title: Content scripts and the isolated world
when: A browser extension must read or change the pages the user visits, and the user needs to know what a content script can and cannot touch.
inputs: what to change on the page
prompt:
Goal: A content script limited to the sites it needs, editing the DOM safely, keeping its styles contained and treating page data as untrusted.
Steps:
1. Static: "content_scripts": [{ "matches": ["https://example.com/*"], "js": ["content.js"], "css": ["content.css"], "run_at": "document_idle" }] with exact hosts.
2. On demand: chrome.scripting.executeScript({ target: { tabId }, files: ["content.js"] }) after a click, using "scripting" plus "activeTab" and no host permission.
3. Isolated world: the script shares the DOM with the page but not JavaScript globals.
4. Mount UI in a host element with attachShadow({ mode: "open" }) so page CSS and your CSS cannot collide; prefix ids and classes.
5. Build nodes with createElement and textContent; never innerHTML with page or remote strings.
6. Single page sites swap content without reloads: a MutationObserver on a narrow container with a debounced handler.
7. Guard double injection: if (!globalThis.__extLoaded) { globalThis.__extLoaded = true; init(); }.
Quality bar:
- Runs only on listed sites.
- Pages look unchanged except the added UI.
Pitfalls:
- "<all_urls>" for a feature used on one site.
- Trusting values read from the page DOM.
- Observing document.body with subtree true and heavy work per mutation.
Verify:
- [ ] Matches name exact hosts.
- [ ] No innerHTML with outside strings.
- [ ] Shadow root or prefixed styles.
- [ ] Double injection guard.
Output: content.js, content.css and the content_scripts or scripting setup in manifest.json.

examples.input: minha extensao precisa adicionar um botao nas paginas de um site
examples.output: content_scripts limited to one host, shadow root UI, textContent only, MutationObserver with debounce, double injection guard
